Augment each passage embedding with a document ID embedding (relative to the current retrieved set) and a sinusoidal passage‑position encoding to inject structural cues. Process the query and enriched passage embeddings jointly through a stack of Transformer encoder layers that use a hybrid attention mechanism: a shared full attention module for global interactions, and a dedicated masked attention module that restricts attention to passages from the same document, to consolidate intra‑document coherence. mechanism_draft.text: Algorithm step: EB-CAR reranker training and inference pipeline. The method operates in two phases. Phase 1 (input preparation): Given a query, a standard dense retriever (Contriever) produces pre-computed passage embeddings and a query embedding from the same encoder. Each passage embedding is augmented with two structural signals: a document-ID embedding (relative to the current retrieved set) and a sinusoidal passage-position encoding, injecting document-identity and ordering cues into the vector representation. Phase 2 (hybrid-attention encoding): The query embedding and the augmented passage embeddings are processed jointly through a stack of Transformer encoder layers. Each layer contains two attention modules: a shared full-attention module that allows global interactions across all passages, and a dedicated masked-attention module that restricts attention to passages sharing the same document ID, consolidating intra-document coherence. The dedicated module is conditionally active, controlled by a configuration flag (use_dedicated_attention); when disabled, only the shared full-attention path is used. The output is a set of contextualized passage embeddings. Phase 3 (contrastive training): The model is optimized with an InfoNCE contrastive loss. The fixed original query embedding serves as the anchor; the contextualized positive passage embedding is pulled closer while negative passage embeddings are pushed away. The training loop computes per-batch loss and averages over the number of batches to obtain epoch-level train_loss and val_loss. The reranker is returned after training. Phase 4 (inference): At test time, dot-product similarity is computed between the static (unchanged) query embedding and the updated contextualized passage embeddings. Passages are ranked in descending order of these scores. The run is identified by a name incorporating the 'hybrid_attention' tag and the configuration state. Supported facets: the conditional branching on use_dedicated_attention, the reranker call signature (query, passage, label, document_id, passage_id, passage_text), the loss averaging, and the weight-loading path are all confirmed by repository evidence. Unresolved facets: the exact sinusoidal encoding parameters, the number of Transformer layers, and the specific masking pattern for the dedicated attention module are not pinned down by the available fragments and remain author-intent descriptions.

mechanism_draft.text: Algorithm step (hybrid-attention encoding): The query embedding and the augmented passage embeddings are fed into a stack of Transformer encoder layers. Each layer applies two attention mechanisms in sequence or in parallel: (a) a shared full-attention module that computes attention over all tokens (query + all passages), enabling global cross-passage interactions; and (b) a dedicated masked-attention module that restricts the attention mask so that each passage can only attend to other passages from the same document, consolidating intra-document coherence. The output of the final layer is a set of contextualized passage embeddings that have absorbed both global and document-local information.
